hypothesis: A restoration-capable Q initialization can retain its goal-zero policy while linked arbitrary-goal stars and intermediate path distances extend the learned relations.
initialization: Audit all saved multi-goal epoch checkpoints and one frozen fixed-goal checkpoint on the same restoration validation cohort. Select by solved count, then long-range solved count, then MAE; restore selected Q and Adam. Record the finite candidate inventory. Comparison is initialization selection, not a matched claim about training regimes.
supervision: Every epoch visits every physical parent once. The same parents face solved and two linked arbitrary targets (distance-stratified target plus another parent's target). Keep the existing balanced restoration replay and all within-shortest-path intermediate pair distances. Arbitrary-goal stars additionally calibrate action edges and rank all six successors. Weighted means preserve the same Huber and soft-ranking objective families; 90% restoration/path and 10% arbitrary-goal weight. No extra prediction head or waypoint search.
split: Preserve the original fixed-goal heldout state mask in every loss, including arbitrary goals, physical edges and intermediate pairs. Whole arbitrary-goal stars containing a heldout state are omitted. New arbitrary-goal evaluation targets are selected from that mask, so all their candidate-to-goal labels remain protected. This is clean for a fixed-goal initialization; a multi-goal initialization did not enforce this historical mask, so any such source must be labeled potentially seen during pretraining.
selection: Five additional exhaustive epochs, primary final checkpoint, no test selection or automatic extension. Save epoch checkpoints, exact parent/global-parent coverage, per-distance errors, shortest-action rates, unrestricted arrival/cycles, and fixed restoration retention. Source and original 100-epoch jobs remain separate.
scope: A bounded merged-supervision continuation, not proof of full-space distance fitting. A smoke run is explicitly not formal training. Detailed results remain outside Git until successful.
